_what: What the literature says about DKK1, read after the EMC reading rather than before it, so the interpretation is not chosen to fit. Every record retrieved this session.
_not_medical_advice: ⛔ Nothing here asserts efficacy, safety, a therapeutic window or clinical readiness for any agent in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma.
_anchor_form: Each record carries `pubmed_url`, the form lint_citations reads.

retrieval.api: Europe PMC REST search, resultType=core, sort=CITED desc, discriminating term in TITLE:()

⭐ what_supports_taking_this_further: The simple Wnt-feedback explanation FAILS ON OUR OWN DATA. DKK1 is a beta-catenin/TCF target (PMID 15592505), so high DKK1 ought to mean active Wnt — yet the beta-catenin-mutant desmoid comparator (PMID 18832571) reads LOW and EMC reads high, separating completely. The observation is therefore NOT accounted for by the standard relationship.

DKK1 is secreted and antibody-accessible with published in vivo anti-tumour effect in another disease (PMID 17068150), and a secreted target is an unusually tractable address in a tumour whose matrix is the standing delivery problem.
⛔ what_argues_against_it_and_is_the_stro: DKK1 IS A MAJOR SKELETAL REGULATOR (PMID 16730481, PMID 16753024). This disease is chondroid. A chondroid tumour reading high for a bone/cartilage gene against five fibroblastic and GIST comparators may be reading LINEAGE, and the literature makes that MORE plausible than it looked before this retrieval, not less.

⚠ THE RETRIEVAL MOVED THE ODDS AGAINST THE INTERESTING READING. That is recorded plainly because the alternative — quoting only the druggability paper — would have been a selection of the literature to fit a result already in hand.
_the_one_observation_that_would_decide: DKK1 in EMC against a CARTILAGE-LINEAGE comparator — conventional chondrosarcoma, or normal cartilage. No series on disk contains one. Until that read exists the row stays `excluded` and the signal stays a lead.

15592505.title: The Wnt antagonist DICKKOPF-1 gene is a downstream target of beta-catenin/TCF and is downregulated in human colon cancer
15592505.why: ⚠ THE STANDARD RELATIONSHIP, AND OUR DATA DOES NOT FIT IT. DKK1 is a downstream target of beta-catenin/TCF — Wnt-induced negative feedback. On that model a tumour with high DKK1 would be a tumour with active Wnt. ⛔ But the beta-catenin-MUTANT comparator in our own data reads LOW DKK1 while EMC reads high, so the simple feedback account does not explain the observation.

18832571.title: Specific mutations in the beta-catenin gene (CTNNB1) correlate with local recurrence in sporadic desmoid tumors
18832571.why: Establishes that the desmoid comparator class is beta-catenin-mutant, which is what makes it a Wnt-activation control rather than just another fibroblastic tumour.

17068150.title: Antibody-based inhibition of DKK1 suppresses tumor-induced bone resorption and multiple myeloma growth in vivo
17068150.why: ⭐ THE DRUGGABILITY HALF. DKK1 is secreted and antibody-accessible, with published in vivo anti-tumour effect in another disease. ⛔ In another disease — nothing here transfers it.

16730481.title: Dkk1-mediated inhibition of Wnt signaling in bone results in osteopenia
16730481.why: ⛔ AGAINST US, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT CITATION HERE. DKK1 is a major regulator of SKELETAL biology. A chondroid tumour expressing it may be expressing lineage, and this makes the unexcluded confound MORE plausible rather than less.

16753024.title: Deletion of a single allele of the Dkk1 gene leads to an increase in bone formation and bone mass
16753024.why: ⛔ Corroborates the skeletal role at the genetic level — the confound is not a technicality.

14695408.title: The role of the Wnt-signaling antagonist DKK1 in the development of osteolytic lesions in multiple myeloma
14695408.why: A worked precedent for tumour-secreted DKK1 driving disease, i.e. the shape of hypothesis this reading would motivate — in a disease with no relation to this one.
